newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks seen rising on growth data.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks seen rising on growth data.

text.p: Chilean stocks could take a bounce from new Central Bank figures pointing to sharply slower economic growth in July, brokers said.

The figures, showing growth down to 5.8 percent in July from 7.5 percent in the same month last year, suggested the economy was slowing down fast enough for the Central Bank to relax interest rates, they said.
"It's quite a bit less than what was expected and it's very possible it will have a positive effect on the market," said Valetin Carril, analyst at Santander Investment.
Most private consultants had growth forecasts at between seven and 7.5 percent.

Combined with recent figures showing lower inflation and higher unemployment, the new numbers signalled the Central Bank's tight-credit policies were succeeding in slowing down the economy and sparked hopes that interest rates would fall.

"This is a very important sign to the market that the (Central Bank) adjustment has hit bottom. For this economy, 5.8 percent is slow," said a broker. The adjustment, or the "ajuste," is the local term for the bank's restrictive credit policies.
Foreign trade figures showing a $267 million deficit in August were roughly in line with expectations and would probably have little net effect on the market, Carril said.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares ended Friday at 98.21 points.
